description: Machine-readable account-wide issue-intake contract owned by spencer-shadley/.github. Version 19 activates the canonical early scope-decomposition checklist item, binds effort to the merged triage-policy rubric, and composes body/checklist/fingerprint evaluation with evaluateTriagePolicy in the verified portable release. The live Issue Form and portable Markdown bodies are deterministic same-repository projections. Consumers admit a release by producer repository, exact source commit and payload digest; they do not author or publish template copies. Live GitHub inheritance of these forms is a producer projection, not proof that Code/CLI consumers have bound adapter-verified evidence. Version 21 moves bounded verification-contract derivation from triage completion to implementation preflight: triage records scope and execution shape, while the implementation owner must derive/persist verification before writer dispatch. Version 22 (code#7074) states outcome/acceptance content as binding and implementation guidance as advisory: 'Durable fix and acceptance' and 'Relevant details' gain inline binding/advisory guidance and an optional worked-examples link, the body validator refuses an empty or placeholder acceptance section and flags file/line-pinned implementation instructions inside it, and triage gains an 'outcome-shaped-acceptance' checklist item. Version 23 is one combined revision (.github#32, #35, #45, #48) published once: (1) the accepted multidimensional taxonomy (code#7586, .github#32: delivers, type, source, effort, priority:repo, priority:fleet, blocked, environment, progress, decomp, resolution) with the completion stamp namespace moving from triaged:vN to metadata:triage-vN and filing defaults agent-review, priority:triage-tbd, progress:triage; (2) the standard `type:proposal` classification (Spencer, 2026-10-04): triage gains a 'proposal-classification' checklist item that applies `type:proposal` alongside the issue's other type labels when the issue proposes a higher-level design or process change whose adoption awaits Spencer's decision; (3) verified direction-impact reconciliation (.github#35): every issue answers the open-ended direction-change question; yes/material impact requires `metadata:direction-change`, exhaustive search of all earlier open issues and PRs across every repository, same-step conflict reconciliation and zero-unresolved-conflict readback. Assessment and verified/resumable reconciliation are bound to independently fetched issue/thread facts through the existing composed evaluator, without granting effect authority; and (4) .github#48: 'Confirm + receipt' admits the `agent_unattested` provenance actor (`triaged-by-<model>-<effort>` is recorded only when an execution or route receipt names the model, and a run without one completes with no `triaged-by-*` label), and a previous or atomic-high effort classification no longer requires a qualified second opinion: it is highly encouraged and checked when recorded, not a completion requirement (see `secondOpinion` in the triage policy). Delta re-triage of revision 22 issues evaluates only added or changed items and their dependents. Bump version whenever this contract or its generated projections change.
requiredHeadings: What happened or what is needed?

workTypes.label: Defect
workTypes.description: Unintended behavior, regression, bug, or contract breach.
workTypes.authority: Direct fix within authorized repository lease; defects require DOCTRINE §14 prevention and §18 detect/heal/recover ladders.

workTypes.label: Task
workTypes.description: Concrete bounded operational or maintenance work without novel architecture.

workTypes.label: Risk reduction
workTypes.description: Proactive hardening, debt reduction, safety guardrails, or vulnerability mitigation.
workTypes.authority: Direct implementation of preventive controls within authorized lease.

workTypes.label: Exploration / design research
workTypes.description: Read-only investigation whose immediate terminal outcome is a proposal/recommendation for an explicit design decision.
workTypes.authority: Read-only investigation and proposal only. Completion never confers implementation authority; separate commissioning required.

workTypes.label: Experiment / evidence test
workTypes.description: Bounded reversible empirical test with declared hypothesis, metrics, exposure/effect/budget/privacy authority, TTL, abort/cleanup and result routing.
workTypes.authority: Bounded empirical test execution strictly within already-authorized boundaries. Classification itself confers no effect or exposure authority.

workTypes.label: Feature
workTypes.description: New capability, user-visible outcome, or functional expansion.
workTypes.authority: Implementation authorized only within explicit scoped specification and lease.

workTypes.label: Mixed
workTypes.description: Multiple work classes combined in one request; triage decomposes or sequences.
workTypes.authority: Requires triage decomposition into discrete bounded work units before execution.

workUnitKey.heading: Governed work-unit key

normalization.sequence: Apply ECMAScript String.prototype.trim(), then String.prototype.normalize('NFC'), then the field-specific case rule.
normalization.fixOwnerGitHubSlug: Apply locale-independent String.prototype.toLowerCase() to the normalized owner/repository GitHub slug.
normalization.workType: Apply locale-independent String.prototype.toLowerCase() to the normalized work type.
normalization.canonicalWorkUnitIdentity: Preserve the normalized UTF-8 bytes exactly after trim and NFC; do not lowercase, collapse internal whitespace, or rewrite punctuation.

workUnitKey.serialization: In identityTuple order, frame each normalized value as its UTF-8 byte length in unpadded ASCII decimal, then ASCII ':' (0x3a), then its exact UTF-8 bytes. Join the three framed values with ASCII LF (0x0a), with no trailing LF. SHA-256 hashes these serialized bytes; render the digest as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
workUnitKey.canonicalIdentity: Choose the smallest durable mechanism or outcome seam that names the work unit. Keep it unchanged when evidence, priority, wording, or comments change.
workUnitKey.collisionHandling: The same key means the same work unit. If distinct semantics would map to one key, resolve the canonical identities before create; never add randomness, a UUID, or mutable evidence to escape the collision.

triageChecklist.heading: Triage checklist
triageChecklist.fingerprintScope: Normalize LF, remove governed-triage-completion markers, trim trailing horizontal whitespace per line, trim the whole body, then append sorted unique triage-owned labels other than metadata:triage-v* / triaged:v* and SHA-256 the UTF-8 bytes.

items.title: Canonical flow
items.text: Use `skills/gh-issue-triage-sweep/SKILL.md`. Keep discovery/orchestration in that skill and selected-collection adjudication in `gh-issue-audit`; do not recreate either procedure in issue prose.

items.title: Value + direction evidence
items.text: Decide current value and direction from live sources. Record `direction-checked-at: <ISO-8601 UTC>` in the idempotent triage receipt, bound to the issue's governed work-unit key and current checklist revision. Direction evidence expires after 3 days. AO #8570 owns runtime stale-evidence re-pend / pickup refusal; Code records the contract and evidence but does not pretend its docs are the actuator. Ask of EVERY triaged issue: "Could this issue materially change direction, i.e. invalidate earlier issues?" The question is open-ended; retirement, SSOT/ownership migration, doctrine, process, taxonomy and learnings are examples, not trigger limits. On yes/potential material impact, apply only the canonical `metadata:direction-change` label (no alias or dual write). Use the reusable Code direction-coherence audit through existing triage. No-impact reasoning can complete without cohort mutations; potential material impact requires an exhaustive search of ALL open issues and PRs created before the causing issue, across EVERY repository, including bodies, acceptance criteria and all comments. Reconcile/rescope or close every conflict in the same audit step, citing the causing issue and accepted decision; refuse completion until exhaustive post-reconciliation readback shows zero unresolved conflicts. Failed, incomplete, unsupported or unknown reconciliation remains explicit and resumable in the existing audit ledger; dispatch alone is not completion. Bind the receipt to independently fetched actual issue/thread and accepted decision identities, normalized scope and current published contract, never labels or matching caller assertions.

items.title: Fix-owner + responsibility
items.text: Resolve fix ownership from the current FleetRegistryReleaseV1 and repository charter evidence. Reuse a prior high-confidence ownership receipt for an existing issue while its durable outcome, repository, relevant scope, and governing charter identity are unchanged. Reroute new work, moves/transfers, cross-repo expansion, ambiguous ownership, charter changes, and catch-all `code`/`agent-orchestrator` cases. An obvious deterministic single-owner result does not require a model seat; use routed judgment only for genuine ambiguity.

items.title: Dedup + queue synergy
items.text: Apply progressive same-class dedupe. Search open work in the resolved owner first and stop when the canonical owner is established. Inspect pending WorkProjection/plan state only when implementation overlap is plausible; search closed history only for regression/prior-fix evidence or when open search is inconclusive; inspect sibling repos only for shared/cross-repo surfaces. Reuse a fresh synergy receipt while issue class, owner, and material scope are unchanged. Never create a parallel implementation track when canonical work already owns the outcome. For potential material direction impact, the exhaustive direction-change gate overrides progressive dedupe stopping rules: search ALL open issues and PRs created before the causing issue across EVERY repository, including bodies, acceptance criteria and all comments, through the same direction-coherence audit. Reconcile/rescope or close each conflict in that same step with the causing issue and accepted decision cited; completion requires exhaustive readback with zero unresolved conflicts. Distinguish obsolete remaining outcomes from valid outcomes superseded and conserved elsewhere; preserve unique acceptance/evidence, exact destination/decision links and active custody. Read the actually published resolution contract immediately before effects; no candidate activation, aliases, dual writes or legacy readiness fallback. Reuse unchanged valid material facts without repeated semantic passes, comments or recursive triggers; changed accepted decisions invalidate only affected obligations and observed result dependents.

items.title: Scope + decomposition
items.text: Resolve work shape before assigning final attributes. Record exactly one current disposition from the canonical triage policy: ordinary leaf (`decomp-not-needed`, low/medium), atomic-high leaf (`decomp-atomic` + `effort:high`; a qualified assessment and an independent confirmation are highly encouraged and are checked when recorded, but completion does not depend on them), or tracking parent (`decomp` + `epic` with a validated child graph). Unresolved or unknown evidence, or a recorded second opinion that fails verification, stays pending. Child triage does not wait for a parent completion stamp. Do not require `decomp-in-progress`. Reuse `evaluateTriagePolicy` and the effort rubric in `contracts/governed-intake-triage-policy.v1.json`; do not copy a second rubric or treat checked boxes as qualified identity. Bind the assessment to the actual server-fetched issue identity and normalized scope using the producer-owned identity API; matching caller-supplied identities or structural checkbox checks alone never establish semantic completion.

items.title: Priority + work dimensions
items.text: Apply the complete priority triplet, exactly one honest effort, and exactly one lawful tier from the live priority/work-spine policies. Effort definitions and examples come from the canonical governed-intake triage policy, not private calibration caps. Missing or unclear effort is unknown, not low. Certified atomic-high remains high. Never self-admit P0.

items.title: Verify + human-required fences
items.text: `tier:auto` executable leaves require a bounded scoped verification contract before an implementation writer starts, but completed triage does not require the issue body to already contain `## Verify`. Reuse a current scoped named-file `## Verify` fence when present; otherwise the implementation commissioning path derives and persists/backfills the verification contract before dispatch. If safe scoped verification cannot yet be derived, the leaf waits on verification clarification at implementation preflight rather than remaining untriaged. Tracking parents do not inherit child Verify, host, or substrate requirements. `human-required` is adjudicated through `stamp-human-required` and requires the current tradeoffs contract. A verification-contract derivation allowance is never blanket body-rewrite authority.

items.title: Cloud vs local execution
items.text: Assess the implementation stage using the [cloud-readiness criteria](https://github.com/spencer-shadley/code/blob/master/docs/architecture/cloud-local-executor-routing.md#cloud-ready-issue-triage). Before triage can complete, apply exactly one execution-substrate label: `cloud-ready` when implementation can run in an authorized provider-hosted environment, or `local-required` when implementation needs a fleet/local machine. Never leave both or neither on a completed triage. Record `ready` or `not-ready`, a short reason, and any separately required local verification/rollout in the existing triage receipt; an unresolved or `unknown` assessment stays untriaged. If one exact host is required, also apply its machine label. Tracking parents do not inherit every child host or substrate requirement.

items.title: Disposition != effect authority
items.text: Adjudicate close / keep / strengthen / residualize / consolidate / move semantics from evidence. Execute close, move, substantive rewrite, or another restricted GitHub effect only when the current role is authorized; otherwise hand the adjudicated effect to the authorized executor with a durable receipt. Do not keep zombie work alive merely because the current seat cannot execute the terminal effect.

items.title: Higher-intelligence handoff
items.text: Unclear effort, `human-required`, material remaining uncertainty, or programme-shaped work uses qualified higher-intelligence assessment inside triage. Scope and decomposition are the earlier `scope-decomposition` obligation. Confirmed tracking parents stay tracking-only. Unresolved delegation is not completed triage. For `effort:high` work, and for an issue that carried `effort:high` before and is now assessed low or medium (it is sized on its current scope), getting a qualified second assessment is highly encouraged (commission the routed assessment seat through `skills/gh-issue-triage-sweep/SKILL.md` and record its receipt), but completion does not depend on it. The triage role does not mint implementation plans or commission implementation writers.

items.title: GitHub effects + quota
items.text: Use the governed GitHub mutation/read path and preserve typed rate-limit defer such as `deferred_rate_limited`; rate-limit or transport failure is not an empty candidate set or successful sweep.

items.title: Confirm + receipt
items.text: Clear pending/legacy triage labels only after the contract is satisfied, then apply the current `metadata:triage-vN` stamp last when authorized and read it back. In addition, a substantive model-triaged run whose model and effort are named by an authoritative execution or route receipt records additive model provenance using `triaged-by-<model>-<effort>` derived from that receipt. A run by an authenticated agent that has no such receipt (provenance actor `agent_unattested`) completes with no `triaged-by-*` label for that run and never invents a model or effort slug. Existing `triaged-by-*` labels are never stripped on re-triage or correction. The single idempotent receipt records checklist completion, direction evidence, disposition, priority/effort/tier, actor-permission outcome, and any handoff. Pickup additionally requires fresh direction evidence. Cosmetic removal of `decomp-in-progress` never gates discovery or reuse.

items.title: Taxonomy
items.text: Validate the current DOCTRINE §14 causal taxonomy and, for defects, distinct prevention and detect/self-heal/recover ladders; conserve new actionable findings as durable work.

items.title: Outcome-shaped acceptance
items.text: Confirm 'Durable fix and acceptance' states binding acceptance criteria (each names a real consumer or the evidence that stands in for one) rather than a prescribed implementation, and that any implementation suggestions live only in 'Relevant details' as explicitly advisory. Rewrite a prescriptive body into this shape using skills/gh-issue-value-review's refresh-required procedure instead of restating it here.

items.title: Proposal classification
items.text: Apply `type:proposal` (from the work-spine type taxonomy, in addition to any other type label) when the issue proposes a higher-level design, architecture or process change whose adoption awaits Spencer's decision; remove it once that decision is recorded on the issue. Bounded defects, tasks and changes agents may decide under standing authority are not proposals. The label is descriptive: it never blocks other work, creates a human gate, or changes priority.

prevention.name: Prevention
prevention.heading: Prevention — never again
prevention.purpose: Never again at each subspecies→domain rank. Distinct from detect/heal/recover.

detectHealRecover.name: Detect / self-heal / recover
detectHealRecover.heading: Detect / self-heal / recover — if it still happens
detectHealRecover.purpose: If it happens: notice, heal, restore, escalate. Distinct from prevention. Do not collapse into a single Fix or next action column.

effortCalibration.description: Effort definitions, conditional examples, unknown handling, and atomic-high remaining-high rules are owned by the canonical triage policy. This contract does not independently cap prevention RCA at medium or force N=1 leaves to low/medium. Missing evidence is unknown, not low.
effortCalibration.decompNotNeededConstraint: Ordinary leaves (`decomp-not-needed`) use low/medium per the canonical policy dispositions. Atomic-high remains high. When decomp/epic is present, remove decomp-not-needed instead of down-calibrating effort (code#6006).
effortCalibration.provenanceEffortCoherence: triaged-by-<model>-<effort> effort slug is the triage seat's execution effort from the route receipt (docs/contracts/issue-triage-provenance.md §4), not a requirement that work-effort labels match (e.g. triaged-by-claude-opus-5-high on effort:medium is lawful; code#6006)

idempotency.description: Governed intake defines a stable work-unit idempotency key and requires it on new bodies to prevent duplicate issue creation.
idempotency.createPathPolicy: Create path searches the target repo for that key before POST. On match of an existing issue, return that URL and do not mint a twin. Search/create failure must not silently mint a second copy of a key that already exists (fail closed or return existing; do not fall through to create on a known key).
idempotency.regressionContract: Two sequential creates with the same key produce exactly one issue, with the second call returning the first issue URL.
idempotency.duplicateHeal: Triage-time close-as-dup remains the heal for pre-key twins; it is not the prevention.
